item.content:encoded:
The University of California President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program (UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program) is an academic fellowship opportunity designed to support outstanding scholars as they prepare for distinguished careers in academia, research, and related fields.

The program provides selected scholars with the opportunity to work with tenured faculty at the University of California, while also offering pathways to additional fellowship opportunities through UC campuses, UC National Laboratories, and partner universities.

For scholars who are interested in pursuing an academic career in the United States, particularly those who have completed a terminal degree and want to strengthen their research and professional experience, the program represents an important opportunity to explore.

The 2026 application cycle opened on September 1, 2026, and the application deadline is November 1, 2026.

What Is the UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program?

The University of California President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program is designed to provide outstanding degree recipients with an opportunity to conduct postdoctoral work alongside University of California tenured faculty.

The broader purpose of the program is to help scholars prepare for careers of distinction in academia and research.

According to the program, the fellowship is open to scholars who hold terminal degrees in their discipline. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to researchers who have reached the advanced academic stage required for postdoctoral research.

The program is not limited to one particular academic field. However, additional opportunities are available through UC National Laboratories that specifically focus on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

What Does the Fellowship Offer?

The program is centered around postdoctoral academic and research development.

Depending on the pathway and institution involved, opportunities can include:

  • Working with University of California faculty members
  • Developing advanced research experience
  • Preparing for an academic career
  • Receiving faculty mentorship
  • Building professional academic networks
  • Participating in professional development
  • Pursuing research within UC National Laboratories
  • Connecting with potential academic career opportunities
  • Developing leadership experience within research and higher education

The program therefore goes beyond simply providing a postdoctoral research position. Its broader purpose is to help scholars develop the experience, mentorship, and professional connections necessary for long-term academic and research careers.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The main UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program states that it is open to all scholars holding terminal degrees in their discipline.

A terminal degree generally refers to the highest degree normally required or recognized for professional or academic practice in a particular discipline. The exact terminal degree can therefore vary depending on the field.

Applicants should carefully review the official application requirements for their particular discipline and proposed research.

Important eligibility points

Applicants should consider the following:

  1. You should hold a terminal degree in your discipline.
  2. Your academic background should be appropriate for the proposed postdoctoral research.
  3. You will need to identify an appropriate UC faculty mentor for the relevant fellowship pathway.
  4. Applicants interested in UC National Laboratory opportunities should have a relevant PhD/STEM research background, as those opportunities specifically seek PhD recipients in STEM.
  5. Partner universities and institutions may have additional eligibility requirements.

Because requirements can differ between the main UC program, Chancellor’s fellowships, National Laboratory opportunities, and partner programs, applicants should not assume that meeting the general UC requirement automatically means they satisfy every partner program’s requirements.

Can International Students and Scholars Apply?

The information provided for the program does not identify the fellowship as being restricted to U.S. citizens or residents.

The main program describes itself as being open to all scholars holding terminal degrees in their discipline.

Therefore, prospective international applicants should review the detailed application requirements and any applicable institutional, employment, immigration, or appointment requirements before applying.

Applicants from countries outside the United States should pay particular attention to the requirements of the specific UC campus, laboratory, or partner institution associated with their application.

What Are UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowships?

An additional opportunity connected to the application is the UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program.

Applicants do not necessarily have to submit a completely separate application for consideration for these UC Chancellor’s fellowships.

According to the program information, applications submitted to the UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program that are highly ranked will also be included in the competition for Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs at the UC campus where the proposed faculty mentor is located.

However, applicants can apply to only one University of California campus.

This means choosing the appropriate UC campus and faculty mentor is an important part of the application process.

Applicants should also consult the individual campus websites because specific Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship awards can have their own requirements and information.

University of California Campuses Participating in Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowships

The UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship programs are associated with the following University of California campuses:

  • UC Berkeley
  • UC Davis
  • UC Irvine
  • UCLA
  • UC Merced
  • UC Riverside
  • UC San Diego
  • UCSF
  • UC Santa Barbara
  • UC Santa Cruz

Applicants should research the campus that is most closely connected to their proposed research and prospective faculty mentor.

UC National Laboratory Postdoctoral Fellowship Opportunities

Another important component of the program is the partnership between the University of California and UC National Laboratories.

These opportunities are particularly relevant to scholars working in STEM disciplines.

The National Laboratory fellowship opportunities combine postdoctoral research with additional professional development opportunities.

According to the program information, the UC National Laboratories seek PhD recipients whose experiences and leadership contribute to:

  • Research excellence
  • Public service
  • STEM research
  • Professional development
  • Mentoring
  • Networking

This creates an additional pathway for qualified STEM researchers interested in conducting advanced research within a national laboratory environment.

Click Here to get access University of California President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program 2026–2027

Which UC National Laboratories Participate?

The program lists three UC National Laboratories associated with these opportunities:

Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is one of the participating laboratories offering opportunities connected to the UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program.

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory also provides postdoctoral opportunities connected to the program, particularly within relevant STEM research areas.

Los Alamos National Laboratory

Los Alamos National Laboratory is another participating laboratory for UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship opportunities.

Applicants interested in National Laboratory opportunities should review the relevant laboratory information and requirements in addition to the central UC fellowship application instructions.

How to Apply for the UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship

Applications for the President’s and Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs must be submitted through the online application portal.

The general application process can be understood through the following steps.

Step 1: Review the program requirements

Before beginning the application, prospective applicants should carefully review:

  • Application instructions
  • Application requirements
  • Evaluation and selection information
  • Terms of award
  • Applicant FAQs

This is especially important because different fellowship pathways and partner institutions can have different requirements.

APPLY HERE

Step 2: Identify your research direction

Applicants should have a clear understanding of the research they intend to pursue during their postdoctoral fellowship.

The proposed research should fit the applicant’s academic background and be appropriate for the UC faculty member or institution with whom they intend to work.

Step 3: Identify a potential UC faculty mentor

Because the program involves working with UC faculty, identifying an appropriate faculty mentor is an important part of preparing the application.

Applicants should research faculty members whose research interests and expertise align with their proposed work.

Step 4: Select the appropriate UC campus

Applicants seeking consideration for UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowships should remember that the program states that applicants may apply to only one UC campus.

Therefore, applicants should carefully consider the campus associated with their proposed faculty mentor.

Step 5: Prepare the application materials

Applicants should follow the official application instructions and prepare all required documents before submitting the application.

The detailed application requirements should be checked directly through the official program portal because requirements may change between application cycles.

Step 6: Submit the application online

The application must be submitted through the official online application system.

Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can submit earlier, particularly because additional information or recommendation letters may have their own deadlines.

Important Dates for the 2026–2027 Application Cycle

Applicants interested in the current cycle should pay close attention to the following dates:

Event Date
Online Application Opens September 1, 2026
Application Deadline November 1, 2026
Letter of Recommendation Deadline December 1, 2026
Decisions Announced March 31, 2027

Application Deadline: November 1, 2026
APPLY NOW

The main application deadline for the UC President’s and Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs is November 1, 2026.

Applicants should ensure that their application is submitted by this date.

The program also specifies a December 1, 2026 deadline for letters of recommendation.

Applicants should therefore begin communicating with potential recommenders well before the application deadline.

What Happens After the Application Is Submitted?

After applications are submitted, they go through the program’s evaluation and selection process.

Highly ranked applications can also be considered for the UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs at the relevant UC campus.

Applicants should understand that the President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship and Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship pathways are connected, but the exact opportunities available to an applicant can depend on factors such as the proposed faculty mentor and campus.

For the 2026–2027 cycle, decisions are scheduled to be announced on March 31, 2027.

Partner Programs Associated With the Fellowship

The UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program also works with several partner programs.

The partnership supports areas including:

  • Postdoctoral research
  • Faculty mentoring
  • Professional development
  • Academic networking

The partner programs are particularly interested in scholars who can bring their leadership and experiences to their academic and research careers.

The listed partner programs include:

  • Cal-Bridge
  • Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center
  • University of Maryland
  • University of Michigan
  • Virginia Tech

The program notes that partner programs can have different scopes and requirements from year to year.

Applicants should therefore visit the individual partner websites to confirm current requirements, deadlines, and eligibility.

Can One Application Be Used for Partner Programs?

The program states that applicants may apply to the University of California, University of Maryland, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, and Virginia Tech President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship programs using the same application.

However, applicants must submit separate mentor letters and research proposals where required.

This is an important point for applicants considering multiple participating institutions.

Using a common application does not mean that applicants can ignore the individual requirements of each participating institution.

Why Mentorship Is Important in This Fellowship

Mentorship is a significant component of the fellowship structure.

The program is designed to give scholars opportunities to work with established UC faculty and develop professionally as researchers and academics.

A strong mentor relationship can help a postdoctoral researcher:

  • Develop research ideas
  • Strengthen academic expertise
  • Build professional networks
  • Gain experience within a research institution
  • Develop an academic career
  • Identify future research opportunities
  • Receive guidance from an established scholar

For this reason, applicants should carefully consider the faculty member they propose to work with and the connection between that faculty member’s research and their own proposed work.

Professional Development and Networking

The program also emphasizes professional development and networking, particularly within its National Laboratory partnerships.

These activities can help postdoctoral researchers expand their professional networks beyond their immediate research group.

Networking can be particularly valuable for scholars planning careers in:

  • Universities
  • Research institutions
  • National laboratories
  • STEM research
  • Academic leadership
  • Public-service-oriented research

The exact professional development opportunities available can vary depending on the fellowship pathway and host institution.

What Fields Can Applicants Come From?

The main President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program is not presented as being restricted to a single academic discipline.

It states that the program is open to scholars holding terminal degrees in their discipline.

This means that potential applicants should examine whether their specific field considers their degree to be a terminal degree and whether their proposed research fits the fellowship and mentor requirements.

The UC National Laboratory opportunities are more specifically focused on STEM, including science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Therefore, STEM researchers may have additional opportunities through the National Laboratory pathway.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be relevant to scholars who:

  • Have completed a terminal degree
  • Want to pursue a postdoctoral research position
  • Are interested in an academic career
  • Want to work with established university faculty
  • Want to develop their research profile
  • Are interested in professional academic networking
  • Want additional research and mentorship experience
  • Are interested in STEM research at a UC National Laboratory
  • Are exploring academic careers in the United States

However, prospective applicants should always compare their individual academic background against the official requirements before beginning an application.

Important Things Applicants Should Check Before Applying

Before submitting an application, applicants should carefully verify the following:

Academic eligibility

Confirm that your degree qualifies as a terminal degree for your discipline and that you meet the applicable academic requirements.

Faculty mentor

Identify a suitable UC faculty mentor whose research interests align with your proposed research.

Campus selection

If pursuing a UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship, remember that applicants may apply to only one UC campus.

Research proposal

Develop a research proposal that clearly fits your academic background and proposed host environment.

Recommendation letters

Contact potential recommenders early and make sure they understand the relevant deadline.

Partner requirements

If applying through a partner program, review that institution’s separate requirements and deadlines.

National Laboratory requirements

STEM applicants interested in the National Laboratory pathway should review the requirements of the relevant laboratory.

Deadlines

Keep track of both the main application deadline and the separate recommendation-letter deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program?

It is a University of California postdoctoral fellowship program designed to give outstanding degree recipients opportunities to work with UC tenured faculty and prepare for distinguished academic and research careers.

Who is eligible for the program?

The main program states that it is open to scholars holding terminal degrees in their discipline. Specific fellowship pathways may have additional requirements.

Is this opportunity only for U.S. citizens?

The supplied program information does not state a U.S.-citizenship restriction. International scholars should nevertheless review the detailed requirements and any institutional or immigration requirements applicable to their appointment.

What is the application deadline?

The application deadline for the 2026 cycle is November 1, 2026.

When does the application open?

The 2026 application opened on September 1, 2026.

When are decisions announced?

For the 2026–2027 cycle, decisions are scheduled to be announced on March 31, 2027.

When are recommendation letters due?

The listed deadline for letters of recommendation is December 1, 2026.

Can applicants apply to more than one UC campus?

For consideration for the UC Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programs, applicants may apply to only one University of California campus.

Are STEM researchers eligible?

Yes. The UC National Laboratory pathway specifically seeks PhD recipients in STEM fields.

Which National Laboratories participate?

The listed laboratories are Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, and Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Are there partner universities and institutions?

Yes. The program lists partnerships involving Cal-Bridge, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, the University of Maryland, the University of Michigan, and Virginia Tech.

How to Access the Official Application

Prospective applicants should use the official University of California President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program website to review the complete application instructions, requirements, evaluation process, terms of award, and FAQs before submitting an application.

Official UC President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program

Applicants should also consult the relevant UC campus, National Laboratory, or partner institution if they are applying through one of those pathways.

Conclusion

The University of California President’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program provides a postdoctoral research and professional development opportunity for scholars who have reached the terminal-degree stage of their academic discipline. The program is designed to connect outstanding scholars with UC faculty while helping them develop research experience, mentorship relationships, professional networks, and preparation for academic careers.

The program also extends beyond the central UC fellowship through Chancellor’s Postdoctoral Fellowships, UC National Laboratory opportunities, and partner programs. STEM PhD recipients may be particularly interested in the National Laboratory pathway, while scholars in other disciplines should investigate the relevant UC faculty and campus opportunities.

For the 2026 application cycle, the online application opened on September 1, 2026, and the main application deadline is November 1, 2026. Letters of recommendation are due by December 1, 2026, with decisions scheduled for March 31, 2027.

Because individual campuses, laboratories, and partner institutions may have additional requirements or different deadlines, prospective applicants should carefully review the official information before submitting their application.

The 4th FAWE International Conference on Girls’ Education in Africa will bring together policymakers, educators, researchers, youth leaders, civil society organizations, development partners, private-sector actors, technology innovators and other stakeholders to discuss how Africa can accelerate progress in girls’ education through sustainable financing, innovation, technology, partnerships and accountability.

The conference will take place in Nairobi, Kenya, from 17–18 November 2026, at the Argyle Grand Hotel Nairobi on Mombasa Road, near Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA). Registration is currently open, with a stated registration fee of USD 100.

The central theme of the conference is:

“Investing in Her Future: Accelerating gender-transformative education for African girls through sustainable financing and innovation.”

The two-day continental convening is designed to move beyond discussion and generate political, financial and institutional commitments that can contribute to stronger and more inclusive education systems for African girls.

About the FAWE International Conference on Girls’ Education in Africa

The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE) is convening the fourth edition of its International Conference on Girls’ Education in Africa as a major continental platform focused on advancing girls’ education.

The conference recognizes that education for girls is closely connected to broader development priorities, including gender equality, economic growth, social cohesion and sustainable development.

According to the conference materials, the event brings together people who shape, finance, research, implement and experience girls’ education. This includes government and policy leaders, development partners, educators, researchers, civil society actors, youth leaders, private-sector partners, technology and innovation actors, and regional and global stakeholders.

The conference is held every three years and is structured around three broad ideas:

  • Political commitment
  • Sustainable financing
  • Innovation

The 2026 edition expands these priorities by incorporating youth leadership, technology, partnerships and accountability.

Conference Theme: Investing in Her Future

The central theme of the 2026 conference is:

“Investing in Her Future: Accelerating gender-transformative education for African girls through sustainable financing and innovation.”

The theme reflects the need to look beyond access to education alone and consider whether education systems are adequately financed, inclusive, innovative and capable of delivering meaningful learning outcomes for girls.

The conference seeks to create a platform where stakeholders can examine how financial resources are mobilized and allocated, how young people participate in decision-making, how technology can improve educational opportunities, and how institutions can become more accountable for results.

Why Is the Conference Being Held?

The conference responds to several challenges affecting efforts to advance girls’ education across Africa.

The conference concept identifies financing, youth leadership, innovation, technology, policy, institutional capacity and accountability as interconnected areas requiring greater attention.

1. Sustainable Financing Gaps

Adequate and sustainable financing remains a major issue in advancing gender-transformative education.

The conference highlights concerns including:

  • Education financing remaining below required benchmarks
  • Limited gender-responsive budgeting
  • The need for more Africa-centered financing solutions
  • Weak expenditure tracking
  • The need for innovative financing mechanisms

The discussions will therefore examine how governments, development partners, private-sector actors and other stakeholders can strengthen financing for girls’ education.

2. Youth Voice and Leadership Gaps

Girls and young people are directly affected by decisions concerning education financing and policy.

However, the conference concept identifies their underrepresentation in policy and governance spaces as an important gap.

The conference therefore aims to elevate youth voices and create opportunities for young people to participate in discussions around:

  • Education financing
  • Policy development
  • Governance
  • Accountability
  • Advocacy
  • Leadership

3. Innovation, Technology and Partnership Gaps

Technology and educational innovation have significant potential to improve access to learning.

However, access to technology remains uneven, and digital solutions do not always adequately address gender-specific challenges.

This is particularly relevant in:

  • Rural communities
  • Fragile contexts
  • Underserved communities
  • Areas experiencing digital inequality

The conference will explore how technology, partnerships and innovation can be used to improve educational opportunities for girls while addressing the barriers that prevent equitable access.

4. Policy, Capacity and Accountability Gaps

The conference also addresses challenges associated with fragmented policies, limited institutional capacity and weak accountability mechanisms.

These challenges can reduce the effectiveness of education financing and programmes.

The conference therefore seeks to strengthen:

  • Policy coherence
  • Institutional capacity
  • Governance
  • Transparency
  • Accountability
  • Monitoring of results

Objectives of the 4th FAWE International Conference

The conference has four central objectives.

1. Mobilize Political, Financial and Institutional Commitments

The conference seeks to mobilize commitments that can sustainably promote gender-transformative education systems.

This includes encouraging political leaders, institutions, development partners and other stakeholders to consider practical approaches to strengthening education for girls.

2. Elevate Youth Voices and Leadership

Another objective is to strengthen the participation of young people in education financing and governance.

The conference recognizes that young people should have meaningful opportunities to contribute to discussions and decisions affecting their education and future.

3. Promote Innovation, Technology and Partnerships

The conference aims to promote innovation and technology that can improve girls’:

  • Access to education
  • Retention
  • Completion
  • Learning outcomes

It will also examine the role of partnerships in scaling successful approaches.

4. Strengthen Policy Coherence and Accountability

The conference seeks to strengthen gender-transformative policies, institutional capacity and accountability mechanisms.

This is intended to contribute to more effective education systems and stronger implementation of commitments.

Four Major Conference Sub-Themes

The 2026 conference is organized around four strategic focus areas.

1. Sustainable Financing for Gender-Transformative Education

This theme examines how education systems can secure and effectively use financial resources to support gender-transformative education.

Topics include:

  • Domestic resource mobilization
  • Gender-transformative budgeting
  • Innovative financing instruments
  • Public-private partnerships
  • Development cooperation
  • Impact measurement

The discussions will consider how financing can be designed to produce sustainable improvements in girls’ education.

2. Youth Voices and Leadership in Education Financing and Policy

This theme focuses on meaningful youth participation in education policy and financing.

Possible areas of discussion include:

  • Youth participation in planning
  • Oversight
  • Leadership development
  • Mentorship
  • Youth-led solutions
  • Accountability
  • Advocacy

The theme recognizes young people not simply as beneficiaries of education systems but also as participants in shaping those systems.

3. Harnessing Technology and Digital Innovation for Girls’ Education

The third theme examines the role of technology and digital innovation in expanding educational opportunities.

Topics include:

  • Inclusive EdTech financing
  • Closing the gender digital divide
  • STEM opportunities
  • Connectivity
  • Data
  • Innovation ecosystems
  • Evidence-based policymaking

The conference will consider how digital tools can contribute to improved access and learning while ensuring that technological progress does not deepen existing inequalities.

4. Gender-Transformative Partnerships, Financing and Accountability

The fourth theme focuses on cooperation between different sectors and institutions.

It includes:

  • Multi-sector partnerships
  • Private-sector engagement
  • Policy coherence
  • Institutional capacity
  • Governance
  • Transparency
  • Shared accountability

The goal is to explore how different stakeholders can work together to achieve measurable progress in girls’ education.

What Will Happen During the Conference?

The conference will follow a two-day programme combining high-level discussions with thematic and youth-focused sessions.

The programme will include:

High-Level Plenary Sessions

The opening and plenary sessions will feature keynote addresses from political leaders, development partners and thought leaders.

These sessions will provide a platform for discussing the broader policy and financing challenges affecting girls’ education.

Thematic Breakout Sessions

Participants will take part in parallel discussions organized around the conference’s four major themes:

  • Sustainable financing
  • Youth voices and leadership
  • Technology and digital innovation
  • Partnerships and accountability

Youth-Led Dialogues

Youth-led sessions will create space for intergenerational conversations around:

  • Education financing
  • Governance
  • Advocacy
  • Accountability
  • Youth leadership

Innovation Exhibitions

The conference will also showcase successful programmes, technologies and financing models that have the potential to improve:

  • Access
  • Retention
  • Completion
  • Learning outcomes

The combination of plenaries, breakout sessions, youth dialogues and innovation exhibitions is intended to connect high-level policy discussions with practical examples and solutions.

Who Will Attend the Conference?

The conference is designed to bring together a diverse continental and international community of stakeholders.

The official conference information identifies the following groups:

Policymakers

Government and policy leaders will participate in discussions concerning education policy, financing and governance.

Development Partners

Development organizations and financing partners will contribute perspectives on cooperation and investment in girls’ education.

Educators and Researchers

Teachers, educators and researchers will contribute evidence, knowledge and practical experiences related to education.

Civil Society Actors

Civil society organizations will bring perspectives relating to advocacy, implementation and accountability.

Youth Leaders

Young people and youth leaders will contribute to discussions concerning leadership, voice and accountability.

Private-Sector Partners

Private-sector organizations can contribute to discussions around innovation, skills and scaling solutions.

Technology and Innovation Actors

Technology organizations and innovators can contribute expertise relating to EdTech, STEM, data and learning systems.

Regional and Global Stakeholders

The conference also brings together regional and international stakeholders interested in continental alignment and advancing girls’ education.

Registration for the Conference

Registration for the 4th FAWE International Conference on Girls’ Education in Africa is currently open.

The stated registration fee is USD 100.

The registration fee provides participants with access to:

  • Plenary sessions
  • Parallel discussions
  • Side events

Early registration is encouraged to facilitate planning and logistics.

The registration form requests information including:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Country
  • Organization
  • Participant category
  • Gender
  • Age range
  • Disability information
  • Conference interests
  • Preferred conference track
  • Message or support needs

The available participant categories include government/policymaker, development partner/donor, educator/researcher, civil society, youth/alumni leader, private sector, media and other.

Conference Date and Venue

The conference will take place on:

17–18 November 2026

The location is:

Argyle Grand Hotel Nairobi
Mombasa Road, Nairobi
Near Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA)
Kenya

The venue is positioned near JKIA, which is relevant for international delegates travelling to Nairobi.

Travelling to Nairobi for the Conference

Delegates travelling to Nairobi are encouraged to make their arrangements early.

The official conference information provides guidance concerning arrival, transportation, accommodation, health, money and other practical considerations.

Airport Arrival

Delegates arriving by air will generally use Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.

FAWE states that it does not facilitate airport pick-up.

Delegates may therefore use reputable transportation options such as:

  • Airport taxis
  • Uber
  • Bolt
  • Little Cab
  • Hotel transfers
  • Other reputable taxi-hailing services

Entry Requirements

African delegates are advised to verify whether they qualify for visa-free or eTA-exempt entry.

Non-African delegates and anyone uncertain about their eligibility should verify Kenya’s current entry requirements through the official electronic travel authorization platform.

The conference website directs delegates to Kenya’s official eTA platform for this purpose.

Accommodation

Delegates are encouraged to arrange accommodation early and follow official FAWE travel guidance.

The conference information indicates that accommodation and help-desk updates will be communicated through FAWE’s conference channels.

Health and Travel Insurance

Delegates are advised to travel with:

  • Appropriate travel insurance
  • Personal medication
  • Emergency contacts

Participants should make their own arrangements before travelling.

Money

Kenya uses the Kenyan Shilling (KES).

Cards are commonly used in hotels and shopping facilities, but delegates are also advised to carry some cash.

Traffic and Transportation

Nairobi can experience significant traffic, particularly during peak periods.

Delegates should therefore allow additional travel time when moving between the airport, accommodation and conference venue.

Exploring Nairobi During the Conference

Delegates who have free time during or after the conference may have opportunities to explore Nairobi and its surrounding attractions.

The conference website highlights several places and experiences, including:

Nairobi National Park

A wildlife destination located close to the city and offering a distinctive urban safari experience.

Giraffe Centre

A conservation-focused attraction in Lang’ata where visitors can learn about giraffe conservation.

Karen Blixen Museum

A heritage attraction associated with Nairobi’s Karen area.

Karura Forest

A natural environment offering walking trails, waterfalls and green spaces.

Maasai Market

A destination for local crafts, beadwork, fabrics and souvenirs.

KICC Viewpoint

A location offering panoramic views of Nairobi when access is available.

Karen and Lang’ata

Areas offering dining, museums, conservation attractions and other leisure experiences.

These activities are optional and are not presented as official conference programme activities.

Partnership Opportunities

FAWE is also inviting organizations interested in partnering with the conference.

Detailed partnership information, packages and collaboration pathways are described as forthcoming.

The current partnership focus includes:

  • Multi-sector partnerships
  • Private-sector engagement
  • Policy coherence
  • Shared accountability
  • Investment
  • Innovation

Organizations interested in partnership opportunities can contact FAWE directly for further information.

Conference Contacts

For conference inquiries, FAWE provides the following official contact information:

Email: girlsconference@fawe.org

Telephone: +254 714 606 629

The conference materials also provide emergency and travel-related contacts, including Kenya’s emergency number and other relevant support contacts. Delegates are encouraged to save important numbers before travelling and verify final logistical information through official FAWE communications.

Important Date to Remember

The conference will take place on:

17–18 November 2026

Unlike an application-based funding opportunity, the conference information provided does not state a separate application deadline. Instead, registration is currently open, and early registration is encouraged for planning and logistical purposes.

Why This Conference Matters for Girls’ Education in Africa

Girls’ education remains connected to many dimensions of Africa’s social and economic development.

The FAWE conference brings several of these dimensions together rather than treating education as an isolated issue.

The focus on sustainable financing recognizes that commitments to girls’ education require adequate and sustainable resources.

The focus on youth leadership recognizes that young people should have opportunities to participate in decisions affecting education policy and financing.

The emphasis on technology recognizes the growing role of digital tools and innovation in education while acknowledging that unequal access can create additional barriers.

The focus on partnerships and accountability recognizes that governments, civil society, development organizations, researchers, communities, young people and private-sector organizations all have different roles to play.

By bringing these perspectives together in one continental forum, the conference seeks to connect political commitment with financing, innovation and practical implementation.

Access the Official Conference Information

Participants can access the official conference platform to review:

  • Conference background
  • Objectives
  • Themes
  • Sub-themes
  • Programme
  • Registration information
  • Travel guidance
  • Partnership information
  • Contact details

The official conference website also provides the conference concept note in English and French.

Conclusion

The 4th FAWE International Conference on Girls’ Education in Africa will take place in Nairobi, Kenya, on 17–18 November 2026, bringing together stakeholders from across Africa and beyond to discuss the future of girls’ education.

Under the theme “Investing in Her Future: Accelerating gender-transformative education for African girls through sustainable financing and innovation,” the conference will focus on four major areas: sustainable financing, youth leadership, technology and digital innovation, and gender-transformative partnerships and accountability.

The event is designed as more than a conventional conference. Its objectives include mobilizing political, financial and institutional commitments, elevating youth voices, promoting innovation and strengthening policy coherence and accountability.

Participants will have opportunities to engage through high-level plenaries, thematic discussions, youth-led dialogues, innovation exhibitions and networking activities.

Registration is open at a stated fee of USD 100, which provides access to plenary sessions, parallel discussions and side events. The conference will be held at the Argyle Grand Hotel Nairobi, near JKIA.

For policymakers, educators, researchers, development partners, civil society organizations, youth leaders, private-sector representatives and technology innovators interested in girls’ education and gender equality, the Nairobi conference provides a platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange, collaboration and engagement around some of the major challenges facing education systems across Africa.

Interested participants should review the official FAWE conference information, confirm the latest registration and travel requirements, and register early to support their participation and logistical planning.

Who qualifies / who can participate?

The conference is open to stakeholders from Africa and beyond. The official registration categories include:

  • Civil society actors
  • Youth and alumni leaders

  • Regional and global stakeholders

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for young people across the Commonwealth to become Wellbeing Champions for the Commonwealth Youth Council’s “Are You Okay?” Campaign, a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health and wellbeing initiative focused on starting conversations, listening to young people, strengthening connections and turning youth voices into meaningful action.

The opportunity is designed for young people who want to make a positive contribution to mental health and wellbeing within their communities. No professional mental health qualification is required. Instead, the Commonwealth Youth Council is looking for young people who care about others, are willing to listen and are committed to helping create respectful and supportive spaces where young people can speak openly about their experiences.

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help bring the “Are You Okay?” Campaign into their own communities. Champions are expected to encourage conversations, connect young people, amplify youth voices and contribute to a wider movement seeking to make mental health and wellbeing more visible across the Commonwealth.

The campaign itself grew out of calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum in Samoa, where participants called for stronger action on youth mental health, including better access to services, mental health education, prevention and support. The Commonwealth Youth Council says the campaign responds by creating a Commonwealth-wide space in which young people can speak, be heard and contribute to action.

Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign will receive certificates of recognition. The current call closes on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST. LinkedIn

Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Official campaign page:
Commonwealth Youth Council – Are You Okay? Campaign

About the Commonwealth Youth Council

The Commonwealth Youth Council, or CYC, is the official representative voice of young people across the Commonwealth.

Established in 2013 with support from the Commonwealth Secretariat’s Commonwealth Youth Programme, the Council works to integrate young people into development processes at national, regional and Pan-Commonwealth levels.

Its work focuses particularly on:

  • Youth representation and advocacy
  • Youth empowerment and development
  • Leadership and skills development
  • Connecting youth leaders across countries
  • Creating opportunities for young people to participate meaningfully in decision-making
  • Supporting youth-led responses to shared global challenges

The Council describes itself as representing more than 1.5 billion young people and works to ensure their perspectives are included in policy and development discussions. Commonwealth Youth Council

The Wellbeing Champions opportunity forms part of that wider youth-engagement agenda.

What Is the “Are You Okay?” Campaign?

The Are You Okay? Campaign is a Commonwealth-wide youth mental health initiative built around a simple but important question:

Are you okay?

Its premise is that young people may frequently respond that they are “fine” even when they are experiencing challenges that remain unseen, unheard or unspoken.

The campaign therefore seeks to move beyond simply asking about wellbeing.

According to the Commonwealth Youth Council, it is intended to create spaces where young people can:

  • Speak about their experiences
  • Be listened to
  • Connect with others
  • Help shape meaningful action around mental health and wellbeing

The campaign is not presented simply as an awareness slogan. It attempts to connect conversations with broader youth participation and action.

Why Was the Campaign Created?

The roots of the campaign can be traced to the Commonwealth Youth Forum held in Samoa in 2024.

Young people participating in the Forum called for stronger action on youth mental health.

Among the issues raised were the need for:

  • More accessible mental health services
  • Better mental health education
  • Greater emphasis on prevention
  • Stronger support for young people’s wellbeing

The Are You Okay? Campaign was developed as a response to those calls.

Rather than treating young people simply as recipients of mental health policies, the campaign seeks to involve them directly in conversations and action.

This approach places youth voices at the centre of the initiative.

The Four Pillars of the Are You Okay? Campaign

The campaign is structured around four simple principles:

ASK — Start the conversation.

This is about taking the first step and creating opportunities for honest conversations about wellbeing.

LISTEN — Hear what young people say.

The campaign emphasizes that asking someone about their wellbeing is meaningful only when people are prepared to genuinely listen to the response.

CONNECT — Make support easier to find.

Young people may need connections to communities, networks, resources or appropriate support.

ACT — Turn voices into action.

The campaign seeks to ensure that conversations about mental health contribute to meaningful responses rather than ending with awareness alone.

The four pillars therefore move from conversation to listening, connection and action.

What Is a Wellbeing Champion?

Wellbeing Champions are young people who help bring the campaign into their own communities.

The Commonwealth Youth Council describes them as young people who take the conversation into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

This means the role is centered on community engagement and peer connection, rather than professional clinical practice.

Champions can help encourage environments in which young people feel more comfortable discussing wellbeing and recognizing that their experiences matter.

The current recruitment call particularly emphasizes three qualities:

Care, listening and commitment.

Candidates do not need to be psychologists, counselors, psychiatrists or other mental health professionals.

Instead, the programme is looking for young people who are willing to engage respectfully with others and support the broader goals of the campaign.

What Will Wellbeing Champions Do?

As a Wellbeing Champion, participants will help take the Are You Okay? Campaign from a Commonwealth-wide initiative into local communities.

The role may involve helping young people:

  • Start conversations about mental health and wellbeing
  • Feel that their experiences are heard
  • Connect with peers
  • Participate in supportive community spaces
  • Share perspectives on the issues affecting their wellbeing
  • Amplify youth voices through the campaign
  • Contribute to locally relevant campaign activities
  • Help turn conversations into broader community action

The campaign language emphasizes creating safe, respectful and supportive spaces for young people to talk, listen and connect.

The exact format of local participation may vary depending on the champion’s community and campaign activities.

You Do Not Need a Mental Health Qualification

One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that applicants do not need a professional mental health qualification.

That means the call is not limited to:

  • Psychologists
  • Medical students
  • Counselors
  • Social workers
  • Public health specialists
  • Mental health professionals

Young people from different academic, professional and community backgrounds may participate.

The Commonwealth Youth Council is explicitly looking for people who:

Care about others, can listen and want to create respectful and supportive spaces.

This makes the opportunity considerably more accessible to young people who may care strongly about wellbeing issues but have not studied psychology, medicine or a related discipline.

A Community Role, Not a Clinical Role

Applicants should nevertheless understand the nature of the position correctly.

Becoming a Wellbeing Champion does not mean becoming a therapist or mental health professional.

The campaign materials describe Champions in terms of:

  • Starting conversations
  • Listening
  • Connecting young people
  • Amplifying youth voices
  • Supporting community engagement

They do not describe Champions as providing diagnoses, therapy or clinical treatment.

This distinction is important.

The role is primarily one of youth engagement, wellbeing advocacy and supportive community connection.

Creating Spaces Where Young People Can Talk

A central idea behind the campaign is that meaningful conversations may help young people feel:

  • Seen
  • Heard
  • Connected
  • Supported

For some young people, talking openly about mental health can be difficult because of:

  • Stigma
  • Social expectations
  • Fear of judgment
  • Lack of trusted spaces
  • Limited awareness of available support

Wellbeing Champions can contribute by making conversations about wellbeing more normal and accessible in their communities.

The emphasis is not on forcing anyone to disclose personal experiences, but on helping create respectful environments where conversations can take place.

Listening as a Core Part of the Campaign

The campaign’s second pillar is LISTEN.

This matters because asking “Are you okay?” without creating space for an honest answer may have little impact.

The campaign therefore emphasizes hearing what young people actually say.

For prospective Champions, this suggests that interpersonal qualities may matter just as much as formal achievements.

Applicants who are patient, compassionate, respectful and able to listen without immediately judging others may be particularly suited to the role.

Connecting Young People

Another campaign pillar is CONNECT.

Mental health and wellbeing support can be difficult for young people to navigate.

The campaign therefore seeks to make support easier to find while building connections among young people and their communities.

Wellbeing Champions may contribute to this by strengthening peer networks and making the wider campaign visible locally.

Again, this does not mean Champions are expected to replace professional services.

Their role is community-oriented and supportive.

Turning Conversations Into Action

The fourth campaign pillar is ACT.

The initiative recognizes that awareness by itself is not necessarily enough.

Young people’s experiences can potentially inform:

  • Advocacy
  • Community activities
  • Youth programmes
  • Policy conversations
  • Future wellbeing initiatives

By participating as a Wellbeing Champion, young people have an opportunity to contribute to a larger Commonwealth conversation about what youth mental health support should look like.

The Wider Are You Okay? Campaign

Wellbeing Champions are one component of a broader campaign.

The official campaign currently includes three major elements.

The PULSE component invites young people to share their experiences anonymously, helping provide a clearer picture of youth mental health across the Commonwealth.

The Wellbeing Champions component mobilizes young people to bring conversations into their communities, connect peers and amplify youth voices.

The campaign also includes a Grand Convening scheduled for 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day.

Together, these elements combine individual experiences, community action and wider Commonwealth engagement.

Certificates of Recognition

The programme offers an additional form of recognition for active participants.

Certificates of recognition will be awarded to Wellbeing Champions who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact through the campaign.

This is important because the certificate is connected to participation and impact rather than simply submitting an application or being named a Champion.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to engage meaningfully if selected.

What Does “Meaningful Participation” Mean?

The current public call does not provide a numerical threshold or scoring system defining meaningful participation.

Applicants should therefore not assume there is a fixed number of events or hours required unless the Commonwealth Youth Council provides additional instructions after selection.

The wording nevertheless indicates that certificates are intended to recognize Champions who actively contribute rather than simply hold the title.

Participants should therefore approach the opportunity as an active community role.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity could be particularly relevant to young people interested in areas such as youth development, wellbeing, public health, community engagement, advocacy, social development, peer support, education, communications or youth leadership.

It can also suit applicants who simply care deeply about how young people in their communities are doing.

A candidate does not need a long professional résumé.

Based on the call, some of the most relevant personal qualities are:

  • Empathy
  • Ability to listen
  • Respect for others
  • Commitment
  • Interest in youth wellbeing
  • Willingness to engage with communities
  • Desire to create supportive spaces
  • Ability to work constructively with other young people

Formal mental health credentials are explicitly not required.

Academic Qualifications

The current Wellbeing Champion call does not specify a mandatory degree or academic qualification.

Applicants are not told that they must:

  • Be university students
  • Hold a Bachelor’s degree
  • Hold a Master’s degree
  • Study psychology
  • Study medicine
  • Study public health

The central qualification described in the call is commitment to supporting young people and participating responsibly in the campaign.

This makes the opportunity potentially accessible to young people with a wide variety of educational backgrounds.

Professional Experience

No minimum number of years of employment or professional experience is stated.

The call does not require previous employment in:

  • Healthcare
  • Mental health
  • NGOs
  • Community development
  • Youth organizations

Previous volunteering, peer support or community-engagement experience may naturally be relevant, but the published call does not make such experience mandatory.

Is This Opportunity Open Internationally?

The opportunity is framed specifically around young people across the Commonwealth.

The Commonwealth currently consists of 56 independent member countries across Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and Americas, Europe and the Pacific.

The call does not provide a separate country-by-country eligibility rule distinguishing citizenship from residence.

Applicants should therefore understand the geographic target as the Commonwealth community, rather than assume it is a completely unrestricted global programme.

Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by:

4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST

Candidates in different time zones should pay attention to the use of British Summer Time rather than assuming the deadline refers to their local midnight.

Because this is a time-specific deadline, applicants are encouraged to submit before the final hours.

Key Information at a Glance

  • Programme: Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions
  • Organizer: Commonwealth Youth Council
  • Focus: Youth mental health and wellbeing
  • Geographic focus: Commonwealth countries
  • Role: Community-based youth wellbeing champion
  • Professional mental health qualification: Not required
  • Main activities: Starting conversations, listening, connecting peers, amplifying youth voices and supporting community action
  • Recognition: Certificates for Champions demonstrating meaningful participation and impact
  • Campaign pillars: Ask, Listen, Connect and Act
  • Grand Convening: 10 October 2026, World Mental Health Day
  • Application deadline: 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST
  • Official campaign page: https://cycofficial.org/are-you-okay/
  • Application: https://lnkd.in/e5ttrdqQ

Why This Opportunity Matter

Mental health discussions are often framed around professional services, but supportive communities can also play an important role in whether young people feel comfortable speaking about the difficulties they face.

The Are You Okay? Campaign takes a youth-led approach by involving young people directly in starting conversations and identifying what support and action may be needed.

That approach also reflects the broader role of the Commonwealth Youth Council, which works to increase meaningful youth participation rather than simply discussing young people without involving them.

For participants, becoming a Wellbeing Champion offers an opportunity to contribute to a Commonwealth-wide initiative while bringing its goals into a local community.

It may also help young people develop transferable experience in:

  • Youth engagement
  • Advocacy
  • Community mobilization
  • Communication
  • Listening
  • Wellbeing promotion
  • Leadership
  • Peer engagement

However, the most important element of the programme remains its central purpose: helping create communities where young people feel able to speak and know that someone is willing to listen.

Conclusion

The Commonwealth Youth Council Are You Okay? Wellbeing Champions 2026 opportunity invites young people across the Commonwealth to play an active role in strengthening conversations around youth mental health and wellbeing.

The campaign is built around four straightforward principles — Ask, Listen, Connect and Act — and responds to calls made by young people at the 2024 Commonwealth Youth Forum for stronger action on mental health.

Applicants do not need professional mental health qualifications. Instead, the Council is seeking young people who care about others, can listen respectfully and are committed to creating supportive spaces within their communities.

Selected Champions will help bring the campaign into their communities, connect young people and amplify youth voices. Those who demonstrate meaningful participation and impact can receive certificates of recognition.

For a young person interested in wellbeing, youth advocacy, community engagement or simply helping create spaces where people feel more comfortable talking about how they are doing, this is an accessible opportunity to participate in a wider Commonwealth movement.

Applications close on 4 October 2026 at 23:59 BST.

 

To explore more global opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation Grant is inviting eligible nonprofit organizations to submit applications for grant funding supporting work in nutrition education, improving access to food, and advancing careers in the culinary arts. Eligible organizations whose missions align with the Foundation’s charitable priorities can submit grant requests for consideration for awards in 2027.

The Foundation has a deliberately focused grantmaking approach, meaning organizations are encouraged to carefully assess whether their primary mission and proposed project directly align with at least one of its three stated areas of giving before applying.

About the Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation Grant

The Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation provides support to qualified 501(c)(3) organizations whose primary missions are consistent with the Foundation’s charitable purpose.

For the current grant cycle, the Foundation is particularly interested in nonprofit organizations working in three key areas:

  1. Nutrition education
  2. Improving access to food
  3. Advancing careers in the culinary arts

The opportunity is therefore particularly relevant to organizations running programs that seek to improve people’s understanding of nutrition, increase access to nutritious or sufficient food, or create educational and career pathways within the culinary sector.

Organizations whose primary missions fall outside these three areas are not considered for funding under this grant opportunity.

Key Areas of Funding

1. Nutrition Education

One of the Foundation’s principal areas of giving is nutrition education. This may include nonprofit initiatives designed to improve knowledge and understanding of healthy eating, nutrition, food choices and related educational issues.

Organizations applying under this area should be able to clearly explain how their work contributes to nutrition education and demonstrate the communities or populations that benefit from their programs.

A strong proposal should establish a clear connection between the organization’s existing mission and its proposed nutrition-related activities.

2. Improving Access to Food

The Foundation also supports organizations whose work focuses on improving access to food.

This area may be relevant to nonprofit programs addressing barriers to food access or working to ensure that communities and populations have better access to food resources.

Applicants should clearly describe:

  • The food-access issue being addressed.
  • The population or community served.
  • The activities being undertaken.
  • How grant funding would strengthen the program.
  • The intended outcomes of the proposed work.

The application should demonstrate a direct relationship between the organization’s work and the Foundation’s focus on improving access to food.

3. Advancing Careers in the Culinary Arts

The third funding priority focuses on advancing careers in the culinary arts.

This area may be particularly relevant to nonprofit organizations providing culinary education, professional development, career preparation, training or other programs designed to help people develop careers in the culinary sector.

Applicants should explain how their programs contribute to career development and what outcomes they expect participants to achieve.

Organizations working in culinary education and workforce development should therefore clearly connect their proposed project to the Foundation’s objective of advancing culinary careers.

Who Can Apply?

The Foundation states that it supports qualified 501(c)(3) organizations whose primary mission aligns with its charitable purpose.

This means the opportunity is intended for nonprofit organizations rather than individual applicants.

Eligible organizations should:

  • Hold qualified 501(c)(3) status.
  • Have a primary mission aligned with the Foundation’s charitable purpose.
  • Work primarily in at least one of the Foundation’s three funding areas.
  • Be able to provide organizational and financial information as part of the application.
  • Submit a grant proposal explaining how the requested funding will be used.
  • Clearly identify the population or communities served.
  • Demonstrate how the proposed program aligns with at least one Foundation focus area.

Organizations whose primary mission falls outside nutrition education, food access, or advancing careers in the culinary arts should not expect their applications to be considered under this focused grantmaking program.

Geographic Eligibility and Countries

The application form includes a country field with a wide range of countries, but the Foundation’s eligibility statement specifically refers to qualified 501(c)(3) organizations.

The 501(c)(3) requirement is a U.S. federal tax-exemption classification. Therefore, applicants should not interpret the country dropdown by itself as establishing worldwide eligibility.

There is no race-based eligibility requirement stated in the published grant criteria. Eligibility is based primarily on the organization’s nonprofit status, mission and alignment with the Foundation’s funding priorities.

For organizations outside the United States, it would be important to confirm directly with the Foundation whether they have an eligible structure or qualifying arrangement before preparing an application.

What Information Is Required?

The online application requires applicants to provide detailed organizational, contact and proposal information.

Applicants should be prepared to provide the following:

Organization Details

The application requests:

  • Organization name
  • Organization EIN/Tax ID number
  • Organization website
  • Main contact’s first and last name
  • Contact person’s title
  • Organization address
  • Country
  • City
  • State
  • ZIP code
  • Email address
  • Phone number

Applicants should ensure that this information is accurate and consistent with their official organizational records.

Grant Amount Requested

Applicants are required to specify the amount of funding being requested.

The application does not, in the provided information, specify a standard minimum or maximum grant amount. Organizations should therefore determine the amount requested based on their proposed project, financial needs and the scale of the activities they intend to undertake.

The requested amount should be clearly explained in the accompanying grant proposal.

Grant Proposal Requirements

A central component of the application is the grant proposal.

The Foundation asks applicants to upload a proposal containing several important elements. The proposal should provide enough information for the Foundation to understand the organization, its work, its financial context and the proposed use of grant funds.

The proposal should include:

1. Brief History of the Organization

Applicants should provide a concise history of their organization.

This section should explain:

  • When and why the organization was established.
  • Its mission.
  • Its primary programs.
  • The communities or populations it serves.
  • The organization’s broader purpose and relevant experience.

The objective is to give the Foundation a clear understanding of the applicant and its existing work.

2. Most Recent Annual Operating Budget

Applicants must provide a high-level overview of their most recent annual operating budget.

The proposal should also identify the organization’s key sources of funding.

This section can help demonstrate the organization’s financial context and provide the Foundation with an understanding of how the proposed grant fits within the organization’s overall operations.

3. Amount Requested

The proposal should clearly state how much funding the organization is requesting.

The requested amount should correspond with the proposed activities and demonstrate a reasonable relationship between the funding request and the anticipated work.

4. How the Funds Will Be Used

Applicants must explain how the grant funding will be used.

This is an important part of the application because the Foundation wants to understand the specific purpose of the requested funds.

Applicants should describe:

  • The activities the funding will support.
  • The intended outcomes.
  • The population being served.
  • The expected impact of the project.
  • How the project relates to the Foundation’s funding priorities.

5. Alignment With the Foundation’s Focus Areas

The proposal must demonstrate alignment with at least one of the Foundation’s three focus areas.

Applicants should explicitly identify the relevant focus area rather than assuming that the connection will be obvious.

For example, an organization may explain how its proposed project:

  • Provides nutrition education;
  • Improves access to food; or
  • Supports education and career development in the culinary arts.

Organizations whose projects address more than one focus area can explain those connections as well.

How to Strengthen Your Grant Proposal

Although the Foundation does not prescribe a specific proposal format in the information provided, applicants can make their submissions easier to assess by organizing the proposal logically.

A well-organized proposal could include:

  1. Organization overview
  2. Mission and history
  3. Programs and communities served
  4. Current need or problem being addressed
  5. Proposed project
  6. Relevant Foundation funding area
  7. Activities and implementation plan
  8. Target population
  9. Expected outcomes
  10. Amount requested
  11. Detailed use of funds
  12. Annual operating budget and funding sources
  13. Expected impact
  14. Conclusion

Most importantly, the proposal should maintain a clear connection between the organization’s mission, the proposed activities, the requested funding and one or more of the Foundation’s stated priorities.

Application Deadline

Deadline: November 1, 2026

All applications must be submitted by November 1, 2026, to be considered for grant awards in 2027.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their proposals. Preparing organizational information, financial details and the grant proposal in advance can help ensure that the application is complete before the deadline.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted through the Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation’s online grant request form.

Applicants will need to provide their organizational details, contact information, requested grant amount and grant proposal.

Questions concerning the application can be directed to grantrequest@abzfamilyfoundation.org.

APPLY HERE

Important Points for Prospective Applicants

Before submitting an application, organizations should consider the following:

  • Confirm that the organization meets the 501(c)(3) eligibility requirement.
  • Review the Foundation’s three funding priorities carefully.
  • Determine which funding area most closely matches the organization’s primary mission and proposed project.
  • Prepare an accurate overview of the organization’s history and mission.
  • Document the communities and populations served.
  • Prepare a high-level overview of the most recent annual operating budget.
  • Identify the organization’s key funding sources.
  • Clearly state the amount being requested.
  • Explain exactly how the grant funds would be used.
  • Define the intended outcomes of the proposed project.
  • Explain how the project benefits the target population.
  • Explicitly demonstrate alignment with at least one Foundation focus area.
  • Upload the required grant proposal.
  • Submit the completed application before November 1, 2026.

Who Is This Opportunity Most Relevant To?

The grant may be particularly relevant to established nonprofit organizations working in areas such as:

  • Nutrition education programs
  • Food education initiatives
  • Food-access programs
  • Community food initiatives
  • Culinary education
  • Culinary workforce development
  • Culinary career training
  • Programs supporting pathways into culinary professions
  • Nonprofit initiatives combining food, nutrition and community development

However, an organization’s work should not merely have a connection to food or culinary activities. The Foundation specifically states that its grantmaking is focused and that it cannot consider requests from organizations whose primary mission falls outside its three areas of giving.

Visit HERE for more information about the Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation Grant 2026.

Conclusion

The Ann B. Zekauskas Family Foundation Grant provides a funding opportunity for qualified nonprofit organizations whose missions align with the Foundation’s focused charitable priorities. The three central areas are nutrition education, improving access to food, and advancing careers in the culinary arts.

For organizations that meet the 501(c)(3) requirement and operate within these areas, the application provides an opportunity to present a specific project, explain the needs of the communities they serve and demonstrate how grant funding could contribute to measurable outcomes.

Prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the Foundation’s eligibility requirements and funding priorities before applying. A strong application should clearly explain the organization’s mission, programs, financial context, proposed activities, intended beneficiaries, expected outcomes and direct connection to at least one of the Foundation’s focus areas.

For more global Grant opportunities, visit OFY HERE.
