item.content:encoded:
The Pure Ocean Call for Projects 2027 is now open for researchers, universities, research institutes and non-profit organizations developing innovative applied research projects aimed at protecting marine ecosystems, conserving biodiversity and improving understanding of the ocean.

The 2027 call is particularly significant because Pure Ocean has established a specific geographical focus: eligible projects must be based in mainland France or French overseas territories. However, the call is open to both French and international ocean researchers, provided their proposed project is located within the eligible French territories.

Selected projects can receive up to €40,000 per year for one or two years, meaning that a two-year project could receive a maximum of €80,000 in funding. Pure Ocean also indicates that support for some projects may potentially be renewed.

The Phase 1 application deadline is October 19, 2026, at 23:59 CET.

About the Pure Ocean Call for Projects

Pure Ocean is an endowment fund created in 2017 in Marseille, France. Its principal mission is to support innovative applied research projects that contribute to the protection of fragile marine ecosystems and biodiversity.

The organization combines research funding with broader efforts to increase public awareness of the challenges facing the ocean. According to Pure Ocean, its activities include supporting scientific projects, organizing conferences, and promoting sporting challenges and other initiatives designed to draw attention to the critical condition of marine ecosystems.

The 2027 Call for Projects therefore provides an opportunity for organizations and researchers working on practical, innovative and scientifically grounded ocean solutions to obtain financial support for projects that can produce tangible and lasting environmental benefits.

What Is the Pure Ocean 2027 Call Looking For?

The 2027 call is built around four major Pure Ocean Challenges, which are based on the United Nations Ocean Decade Challenges.

Applicants should develop projects that address one or more of these areas.

1. Understanding Marine Pollution and Tackling It at the Source

Marine pollution is one of the major pressures affecting ocean ecosystems. Pollution can originate from multiple sources, including human activities on land and at sea.

Pure Ocean is seeking research that can improve understanding of marine pollution and contribute to practical solutions for preventing or reducing pollution at its source.

Potential areas of research may include:

  • Understanding the causes and pathways of marine pollution
  • Studying the effects of pollutants on marine organisms and ecosystems
  • Developing innovative approaches to reduce pollution
  • Identifying technologies or methods for preventing pollution
  • Investigating the long-term effects of pollutants
  • Developing solutions that can be applied beyond a single research site

The emphasis is on research that can contribute to meaningful and practical action rather than projects limited solely to awareness activities.

2. Protecting Biodiversity and Restoring Degraded Marine Ecosystems

Marine biodiversity is another central focus of the Pure Ocean programme.

Projects may seek to improve understanding of marine species, protect vulnerable ecosystems or develop approaches for restoring marine environments that have been degraded.

Relevant projects could involve:

  • Conservation of marine species
  • Restoration of degraded ecosystems
  • Protection of important marine habitats
  • Understanding changes in marine biodiversity
  • Development of innovative restoration techniques
  • Monitoring marine ecosystems
  • Research into the relationships between species and their environments

Pure Ocean’s previous supported projects demonstrate the organization’s interest in practical research that can contribute to biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

3. Building Resilience and Adaptation to Climate Change

Climate change is placing increasing pressure on marine ecosystems and the communities that depend on them.

The 2027 call therefore supports research addressing resilience and adaptation to climate change.

Projects may explore how marine ecosystems respond to environmental changes and how conservation and management approaches can help ecosystems become more resilient.

Research could potentially examine:

  • Climate-related changes in marine ecosystems
  • Adaptation strategies
  • Ecosystem resilience
  • Effects of changing environmental conditions on marine species
  • Nature-based approaches to climate adaptation
  • Strategies for protecting vulnerable marine habitats
  • Interactions between climate change and biodiversity loss

Applicants should demonstrate how their research can contribute to practical and lasting solutions.

4. Improving Understanding of the Ocean System

The fourth Pure Ocean Challenge focuses on improving scientific understanding of the ocean system.

The ocean is an interconnected system in which biological, physical and chemical processes influence one another. Better scientific understanding can therefore support improved conservation and management.

Projects under this theme may seek to:

  • Improve understanding of marine ecosystems
  • Study marine organisms and their environments
  • Monitor changes in ocean conditions
  • Investigate interactions between marine systems
  • Improve methods for observing and measuring changes in the ocean
  • Generate scientific evidence that can support future conservation action

Pure Ocean explains that its supported projects can contribute to observing and measuring changes in marine life and physical and chemical characteristics, using marine resources sustainably, and identifying techniques for restoring ecosystems and biodiversity.

Where Must the Project Be Based?

One of the most important changes or conditions for the 2027 call is the geographical focus.

For this year’s call, projects must be based exclusively in mainland France or French overseas territories.

The eligible geographical areas include:

  • The French Atlantic coast
  • French overseas territories in the Atlantic
  • The Mediterranean
  • The French Southern and Antarctic Lands
  • French overseas territories in the Indian Ocean
  • French overseas territories in the Pacific

This geographical requirement is particularly important for applicants outside France.

For example, an international researcher may be eligible to apply if they are developing an eligible ocean research project based in one of the qualifying French territories. Pure Ocean explicitly states that it welcomes French or international ocean researchers with a project based in France.

Therefore, being from another country does not automatically prevent an applicant from participating. The key geographical requirement is where the proposed project will be implemented.

Who Can Apply?

The Pure Ocean 2027 Call for Projects is aimed primarily at organizations and researchers involved in ocean science, marine conservation and related applied research.

According to the official eligibility requirements, only non-profit organizations can apply and receive funding. These include:

  • Universities
  • Research institutes
  • Non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
  • Other eligible non-profit organizations

A project can nevertheless involve collaboration with private-sector organizations, including companies and startups. However, the applicant receiving the Pure Ocean funding must be an eligible non-profit organization.

International Researchers Are Welcome

The call is not restricted to French nationals.

Pure Ocean specifically states that international or French ocean researchers are welcome to submit proposals when the project is based in France.

This means that researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Oceania and other parts of the world may potentially participate, provided that the project meets the geographical and organizational requirements.

The important distinction is between the nationality or origin of the researcher and the location of the project.

For 2027:

Researcher: May be French or international.

Organization: Must be an eligible non-profit organization capable of applying for and receiving the funding.

Project location: Must be mainland France or an eligible French overseas territory.

Is There an Age Limit?

There is no age limit for applicants under the 2027 call.

However, Pure Ocean particularly encourages researchers who are at an early stage of their careers to apply.

This makes the opportunity potentially relevant to emerging researchers as well as more established research teams, provided that the project satisfies the other eligibility requirements.

What Types of Projects Are Not Eligible?

Not every ocean-related initiative qualifies for funding.

Pure Ocean states that funding cannot be used exclusively for:

  • Awareness-raising projects
  • Clean-up initiatives
  • Events
  • Art projects
  • Advocacy projects
  • Training projects

For-profit, promotional and advertising projects are also outside the scope of the call.

This distinction is important.

For example, an organization might conduct an ocean awareness campaign or organize a beach-cleaning event, but an initiative consisting exclusively of those activities would not meet the research focus of this funding opportunity.

The call is designed around innovative applied research capable of producing tangible environmental and scientific impact.

How Much Funding Is Available?

Selected projects can receive:

Up to €40,000 per year

for a project lasting:

One to two years.

Consequently, a two-year project can receive up to:

€80,000 in total.

The final amount and duration are determined by Pure Ocean’s Scientific Committee.

Pure Ocean also states that support for certain projects may be renewed.

Applicants should therefore develop a realistic project budget that clearly connects the requested funding to the project’s activities, research methodology and expected results.

What Does Pure Ocean Look for in Applications?

The principal evaluation criterion is impact.

Pure Ocean describes impact as the tangible and lasting benefit produced by implementing the project within one or more of the Pure Ocean Challenges.

The Scientific Committee evaluates proposals using five equally weighted criteria.

1. Innovation

The project should present an innovative approach to addressing an ocean challenge.

Pure Ocean identifies several forms of innovation, including:

  • Technological innovation
  • Social innovation
  • Nature-based or biomimetic innovation
  • Exploratory innovation

Applicants should clearly explain what makes their proposed approach different or innovative.

2. Relevance

The proposal should directly address one or more of the four Pure Ocean Challenges.

Applicants should establish a clear connection between the research problem and the specific ocean challenge being addressed.

A strong proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand:

  • What problem is being addressed?
  • Why does it matter?
  • Which Pure Ocean Challenge does it address?
  • How will the research contribute to solving the problem?

3. Consistency

The project’s objectives and methods must be clearly defined and achievable within the proposed timeframe.

Applicants should demonstrate that the project is realistic in terms of:

  • Research objectives
  • Methodology
  • Available resources
  • Timeline
  • Expected outputs
  • Funding requirements

The proposal should show a logical connection between the identified problem, research methods, activities and expected outcomes.

4. Collaboration

Pure Ocean places importance on collaboration.

Projects should involve active participation from several stakeholders and encourage interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary approaches.

Depending on the nature of the research, collaboration could involve:

  • Researchers
  • Universities
  • NGOs
  • Conservation organizations
  • Local stakeholders
  • Public institutions
  • Communities
  • Private-sector organizations
  • Technical experts

Private-sector organizations may participate as collaborators even though for-profit entities cannot themselves receive the Pure Ocean funding as the primary applicant.

5. Multiplication and Dissemination

Research should not simply remain inside a laboratory or academic publication.

Pure Ocean wants projects to include a plan for disseminating results to appropriate audiences and engaging those audiences.

Applicants should therefore consider how findings will reach relevant stakeholders, which could include:

  • Researchers
  • Policymakers
  • Conservation organizations
  • Local communities
  • Industry
  • Students
  • Environmental organizations
  • The general public

The dissemination strategy should be appropriate to the project’s target audiences.

How Does the Application Process Work?

The 2027 Pure Ocean Call for Projects uses a two-phase selection process.

Phase 1: Initial Application

Phase 1 is open to applicants who meet the eligibility requirements.

Applicants are asked to complete a short online form presenting the general outline of their proposed project.

The Phase 1 application includes information such as:

  • The main idea of the project
  • The project leader
  • The organization
  • A graphical abstract
  • Keywords

This first stage is designed to provide Pure Ocean with an initial understanding of the proposed research and its relevance to the call.

Phase 2: Full Proposal

Following Phase 1, 20 selected applicants will advance to Phase 2.

Those applicants will be invited to submit a more detailed proposal.

The Phase 2 application provides an opportunity for Pure Ocean to evaluate the project more deeply, including:

  • The research context
  • Project objectives
  • Methodology
  • Expected impacts
  • Outreach and dissemination strategy

Applicants who progress to this stage should be prepared to provide a substantially more developed description of their research.

Important 2027 Application Deadlines

Applicants should carefully follow the official timetable.

Key dates

September 21, 2026:
The 2027 Call for Projects opens.

October 19, 2026, at 23:59 CET:
Phase 1 application deadline.

October 30, 2026:
Qualified applicants are expected to be notified about progression to Phase 2 by this date at the latest.

November 2, 2026:
Phase 2 opens.

December 7, 2026, at 23:59 CET:
Final application deadline for the call.

Mid-February 2027:
The 10 finalists will be contacted.

March 21, 2027:
Pure Ocean plans to announce the selected grantees.

The immediate deadline to remember

For applicants considering this opportunity now, the most important immediate date is:

October 19, 2026 at 23:59 CET — Phase 1 closes.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to prepare their submissions because the first phase requires the project concept, organization information, project leader details, graphical abstract and keywords.

Language of the Application

The application form must be completed in English only.

Pure Ocean also states that incomplete applications will be disqualified.

Applicants should therefore carefully review the online form before submission and ensure that all required sections have been completed.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although the final decision rests with Pure Ocean’s Scientific Committee, applicants can use the published evaluation criteria to structure their proposals.

A potential applicant should begin by identifying a clearly defined marine or ocean-related problem.

The proposal should then demonstrate:

  1. The problem — What marine challenge is being addressed?
  2. The evidence — What scientific evidence demonstrates that the problem exists?
  3. The innovation — What new or innovative approach will be used?
  4. The location — Where in mainland France or a French overseas territory will the project take place?
  5. The methodology — How will the research be conducted?
  6. The collaboration — Which organizations, researchers or stakeholders will participate?
  7. The impact — What tangible and lasting change could the project produce?
  8. The dissemination — How will the research findings reach relevant audiences?
  9. The timeline — Can the objectives realistically be achieved within one or two years?
  10. The budget — Is the requested funding clearly connected to the proposed activities?

Applicants should also ensure that the project does not fall into one of the excluded categories.

Why the Geographic Requirement Matters

The 2027 geographic focus represents an important consideration for international applicants.

Pure Ocean has previously supported projects in different parts of the world, and its portfolio includes projects associated with countries and regions outside France. However, the 2027 call specifically limits eligible projects to mainland France and French overseas territories.

Therefore, an organization based outside France should not assume that its location automatically makes it ineligible.

Instead, the critical question is:

Is the proposed project itself based in an eligible French territory?

An international research team could potentially participate where its project meets this requirement and the application is submitted through an eligible non-profit organization.

Examples of Research Areas That Could Align With the Call

The four Pure Ocean Challenges create a broad framework for eligible research.

Potential areas of work could include:

  • Marine plastic pollution
  • Marine ecosystem restoration
  • Conservation of threatened marine species
  • Climate resilience of marine ecosystems
  • Ocean observation
  • Marine biodiversity monitoring
  • Sustainable use of marine resources
  • Innovative marine conservation technologies
  • Nature-based marine solutions
  • Marine ecosystem health
  • Ocean-system research
  • Pollution prevention
  • Restoration of degraded habitats
  • Research into climate-related impacts on marine ecosystems

However, an applicant should not rely solely on the subject matter of a project.

The proposal must also demonstrate innovation, relevance, consistency, collaboration and a plan for multiplication or dissemination, because these are the published evaluation criteria.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly relevant to:

  • Ocean researchers
  • Marine scientists
  • Universities
  • Research institutes
  • Marine conservation NGOs
  • Environmental non-profit organizations
  • Interdisciplinary research teams
  • Early-career researchers
  • Organizations developing innovative marine conservation solutions
  • Researchers working on marine biodiversity
  • Researchers studying ocean pollution
  • Scientists researching climate resilience in marine ecosystems

Organizations considering an application should first confirm that they meet the non-profit requirement and that their proposed project will be implemented in an eligible French location.

APPLY HERE

Further Information

The official Pure Ocean page provides the complete 2027 Call for Projects information, including eligibility requirements, evaluation criteria, timetable and application instructions.

MORE ON PURE OCEAN 2027 CLICK HERE

For questions about the call, Pure Ocean lists its scientific coordinator’s contact as science@pure-ocean.org.

Conclusion

The Pure Ocean Call for Projects 2027 provides an opportunity for eligible non-profit organizations, universities, research institutes and NGOs to obtain funding for innovative applied research addressing major challenges facing the ocean.

The call is organized around four central themes: understanding and tackling marine pollution, protecting biodiversity and restoring degraded ecosystems, building resilience and adaptation to climate change, and improving scientific understanding of the ocean system.

Selected projects can receive up to €40,000 per year for one or two years, with a maximum potential award of €80,000 for a two-year project. The call does not impose an age limit and particularly encourages early-career researchers.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the 2027 geographic restriction. Projects must be based in mainland France or eligible French overseas territories, even though Pure Ocean welcomes both French and international ocean researchers.

The first stage of the application process closes on October 19, 2026, at 23:59 CET. Applications must be completed in English, and incomplete submissions will be disqualified.

For researchers and organizations developing scientifically credible, innovative and practical solutions for marine conservation, the call offers an opportunity to connect research with tangible action for the protection of ocean ecosystems and biodiversity.

Applicants should consult the official Pure Ocean website and application platform for the most current requirements before submitting their proposals.

item.content:encoded:
Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship offers international students an outstanding opportunity to pursue a fully funded master’s degree in Europe. The prestigious programme supports highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA who wish to pursue an eligible full-time master’s degree at Maastricht University in the Netherlands.

Offered by Maastricht University (UM), the NL-High Potential Scholarship programme is designed for highly talented international students who want to pursue a full-time master’s degree at Maastricht University. The programme combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the NL Scholarship, financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science in cooperation with Dutch universities and universities of applied sciences.

The scholarship is particularly significant because it provides extensive financial support covering major study and living costs. Based on the published scholarship structure, support includes a tuition fee waiver, living expenses, health and liability insurance, visa-related costs, Pre-Academic Training costs and certain International Student Ambassador Programme costs.

Maastricht University states that the programme offers 21 full scholarships each academic year, making this an exceptionally attractive but highly competitive opportunity.

Prospective applicants should also understand that selection is extremely competitive. Maastricht University states that only around 2% of applicants are ultimately awarded the scholarship.

Applications are open from 1 October 2026 until 1 February 2027 23:59 CET.

About Maastricht University

Maastricht University is located in Maastricht, the Netherlands, and provides undergraduate, graduate and research opportunities across a variety of academic disciplines.

Through the NL-High Potential Scholarship programme, the university seeks to attract academically outstanding students from outside the European Union and European Economic Area who demonstrate strong potential to succeed in one of its participating master’s programmes.

Successful scholarship recipients do more than receive financial assistance. Awardees are also expected to become active ambassadors for Maastricht University and the NL-High Potential Scholarship programme during and after their studies.

What Is the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship?

The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship is a competitive funding programme for talented international students admitted to eligible full-time master’s programmes at Maastricht University.

The programme consists of two scholarship components:

  1. The High Potential Scholarship, funded through the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund.
  2. The NL Scholarship, financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with participating Dutch higher education institutions.

The programme is intended to make it possible for outstanding international students to undertake a full degree programme in the Netherlands.

The scholarship is comprehensive because it addresses several of the largest financial barriers international students encounter when studying overseas, including tuition, accommodation and everyday living expenses.

Number of Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarships Available

Maastricht University offers 21 full scholarships each academic year under the programme.

The limited number of awards is important for prospective applicants to consider when preparing their applications.

Maastricht University explicitly describes the programme as highly competitive and indicates that approximately 2% of applicants receive the scholarship.

Applicants should therefore devote substantial attention to academic performance, their motivation letter, CV, supporting documentation, reference letter and the overall quality and completeness of their application.

Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship Benefits

The scholarship provides substantial financial assistance to successful recipients.

Based on the currently published scholarship amounts, funding covers the following areas:

1. Living Expenses

For a one-year programme lasting 13 months, the published living-expense allowance is:

€20,150

For a two-year programme lasting 25 months, the published living-expense allowance is:

€38,750

The living allowance is paid to scholarship recipients by the Maastricht University International Services Desk.

The university indicates that the 13-month living allowance corresponds to approximately €1,550 per month.

Applicants preparing for the 2027–2028 academic year should note that the published financial amounts are subject to change.

2. Full Tuition Fees

Tuition fees are covered at cost and are arranged and paid by the Maastricht University International Services Desk.

This is one of the most significant benefits of the scholarship because successful recipients do not have to independently fund the applicable Maastricht University tuition fees covered by the award.

3. Health and Liability Insurance

The published scholarship package allocates approximately:

€700

towards health and liability insurance.

The insurance is arranged and paid for by the UM International Services Desk.

4. Visa Application Costs

Applicable visa application costs are covered at cost.

The Maastricht University International Services Desk arranges and pays these costs as part of the scholarship package.

5. Pre-Academic Training Costs

The cost of the required Pre-Academic Training is also covered at cost and arranged by the UM International Services Desk.

6. International Student Ambassador Programme

The scholarship also covers the applicable costs for the first block of the International Student Ambassador Programme.

Applicants should remember that scholarship amounts and financial arrangements published for one academic cycle can change for the following academic year. Candidates for the 2027–2028 cycle should therefore verify the final amounts when Maastricht University publishes the updated scholarship information.

How the Living Allowance Is Calculated

Maastricht University provides a useful breakdown illustrating how the published monthly living allowance may be allocated.

Based on the €1,550 monthly figure, the indicative expenses include:

  • Housing: €960 per month
  • Groceries and personal hygiene: €160 per month
  • Telephone: €60 per month
  • Travel: €100 per month
  • Books and study materials: €90 per month
  • Clothing, hobbies and going out: €125 per month
  • Miscellaneous expenses: €55 per month

These figures demonstrate that the living allowance is intended to support both accommodation and normal day-to-day student expenses.

The amounts are subject to change, so future applicants should use them as an indication of the scholarship’s financial structure rather than assume that the exact figures will necessarily remain unchanged for the 2027–2028 academic year.

Are Air Tickets Covered?

No. Applicants should budget separately for international travel.

The scholarship information specifically states that air tickets are not included and must be paid for by the candidate.

Prospective students should therefore factor airfare and any other personal travel costs not included in the scholarship into their financial planning.

Important Accommodation Requirement

One particularly important condition of the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship concerns accommodation.

A room allocated to the successful candidate forms a mandatory part of the scholarship.

Accepting the scholarship means accepting the allocated accommodation.

Candidates cannot simply reject the room and keep the remainder of the scholarship. Refusing the allocated room results in cancellation of the scholarship.

Applicants should also understand that the accommodation provided to scholarship students is not suitable for partners, spouses or children.

The university indicates that relevant accommodation preferences, including preferences associated with religious beliefs, can be taken into account.

Candidates who intend to relocate with family members should therefore carefully consider this requirement before applying.

Duration of the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship

The duration of financial support depends on the length of the master’s programme.

The scholarship is provided for:

  • 13 months for a one-year master’s programme.
  • 25 months for a two-year master’s programme.

Applicants should therefore check the duration of their intended Maastricht University programme when considering the overall value and length of the scholarship.

Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy all applicable scholarship and university admission requirements.

Among the major requirements, candidates must have an eligible nationality and immigration status, apply for an eligible full-time Maastricht University master’s programme and demonstrate excellent previous academic performance.

Applicants must also meet the specific admission requirements of the master’s programme for which they are applying.

Candidates should pay particular attention to the following conditions:

Nationality Requirement

Applicants must hold the nationality of a country outside the European Union/European Economic Area, Switzerland and Surinam and satisfy the applicable requirements for obtaining a Dutch entry visa and residence permit.

Applicants must not hold dual nationality from an EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

Candidates should carefully check the visa and residence requirements applicable to their circumstances.

Master’s Programme Requirement

Candidates must apply for admission to a participating full-time Maastricht University master’s programme for the relevant academic year.

Not every master’s programme at Maastricht University is necessarily eligible for the scholarship.

Prospective candidates must therefore check the university’s official list of participating programmes for the academic year in which they intend to begin their studies.

Academic Admission Requirements

Applicants must satisfy the specific admission requirements of their chosen Maastricht University master’s programme.

Applying for the scholarship does not replace the normal university admission process.

Previous Study in the Netherlands

Candidates must not previously have participated in a degree-seeking higher education programme in the Netherlands.

However, students who previously completed an exchange programme in the Netherlands are permitted to apply.

Previous Master’s Degree

Preference is given to applicants who have not already obtained a master’s degree.

Age Requirement

For the published 2026–2027 cycle, applicants were required to be no older than 35 years of age on 1 September 2026.

Prospective applicants for 2027–2028 should confirm the corresponding age cut-off when Maastricht University publishes the updated application conditions.

Academic Excellence Requirement

Academic excellence is a central selection requirement.

Under the published criteria, candidates must demonstrate outstanding results from previous education through their latest academic transcript.

The required benchmark is a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10, or its recognised equivalent.

Maastricht University explains that this can correspond to:

  • At least 75% out of 100%, or
  • Approximately 3 out of 4 under an applicable grading system.

Applicants must provide official evidence of their GPA and documentation explaining the grading system used by their university.

Ambassador Commitment

Successful candidates must agree to become active ambassadors for the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship and Maastricht University.

This commitment applies during and after their studies.

Recipients are expected to share their experiences during at least one information session for students and/or other stakeholders.

How to Apply for the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship

The application process involves both applying for an eligible master’s programme and submitting a separate scholarship application.

Candidates should not treat these as interchangeable processes.

Step 1: Apply for an Eligible Maastricht University Master’s Programme

The first major step is to select and apply for a participating master’s programme at Maastricht University.

Applicants submit their programme application through Studielink.

After the programme application has been submitted, the candidate receives a Maastricht University student ID number.

This student number is important because it is required to complete and submit the scholarship application.

Candidates should verify that their chosen master’s degree appears on the official list of programmes participating in the NL-High Potential Scholarship for their intended academic year.

For further details on how to apply for a master programme at UM, please see your prospective programme’s webpage

Step 2: Complete the Scholarship Application Form

Once the applicant has received a Maastricht University account/student number, the candidate can proceed with the dedicated scholarship application.

The scholarship application must be submitted through Maastricht University’s designated application form.

Candidates should carefully prepare all required materials before submission.

The university states that candidates can submit their application only once and for one scholarship only. Documents cannot simply be added or replaced after the application has been submitted.

This makes document preparation particularly important.

Please fill out the application form here

Documents Required for the Scholarship Application

Applicants should prepare a comprehensive application package.

The published requirements include the following:

1. Curriculum Vitae

Candidates must submit an up-to-date CV containing relevant information about their:

  • Education
  • Employment or professional experience
  • Academic background
  • Relevant accomplishments
  • Awards and prizes, where applicable

The CV should not exceed two A4 pages.

Applicants who have received academic awards, professional recognition or other relevant prizes should include them.

2. Motivation Letter

Applicants must submit a scholarship motivation letter using the template provided by Maastricht University.

The letter is intended to explain the candidate’s motivation for receiving the scholarship.

Because competition is extremely high, applicants should ensure that their motivation is clearly expressed and supported by relevant evidence from their academic, professional or personal experiences.

3. Proof of Academic Excellence

Candidates must provide evidence demonstrating that they satisfy the scholarship’s academic standard.

This includes:

  1. A university transcript or official document from the applicant’s home university showing the most recent GPA.
  2. A document explaining the grading system used by the applicant’s university.

Under the published requirements, only candidates meeting the equivalent of at least 7.5 out of 10 are considered.

4. Personal Statement of Financial Needs

Applicants must submit a statement explaining why receiving the scholarship would benefit them financially.

Candidates may describe relevant personal circumstances that demonstrate financial need.

The purpose is to give the selection committee meaningful context about why scholarship funding is important to the applicant’s ability to pursue the programme.

Applicants should provide an accurate and genuine account of their circumstances rather than relying on generic statements.

5. Reference Letter

A reference letter is another mandatory part of the application package.

Eligible referees can include:

  • Current or former professors
  • Lecturers
  • Employers

Family members cannot serve as referees.

Applicants must ensure that the reference letter follows Maastricht University’s scholarship reference-letter guidelines.

The published 2026–2027 requirements also specified that recommendation letters needed to be appropriately dated and compliant with the university’s guidelines.

Candidates applying for the next cycle should check the updated reference-letter date requirements when applications reopen.

Importantly, the applicant is responsible for uploading the reference letter.

The referee does not upload it separately.

6. Referee Contact Details

Candidates must also supply contact information for one referee.

The required information includes:

  • The referee’s relationship to the applicant
  • The referee’s work telephone number, including the relevant international calling code
  • The referee’s work or institutional email address

The university may contact referees to verify authenticity.

Candidates should therefore ensure that the information is correct and that the referee is aware of the application.

A personal email address alone does not satisfy the published referee-email requirement; applicants should provide the referee’s professional or institutional email address.

Important Application Rules

Applicants should carefully follow all instructions because incomplete or incorrectly submitted applications can affect eligibility.

Important rules include:

  1. Apply for a participating master’s programme before proceeding with the scholarship application.
  2. Obtain the Maastricht University student ID required for the scholarship form.
  3. Make sure the selected programme participates in the scholarship scheme.
  4. Prepare all required documents before submitting the scholarship application.
  5. Ensure academic documents clearly demonstrate the required GPA or equivalent.
  6. Include official documentation explaining the applicant’s university grading system.
  7. Follow the required motivation-letter template.
  8. Follow the official reference-letter guidelines.
  9. Provide legitimate professional or institutional referee contact information.
  10. Review every uploaded document carefully before final submission.

Applicants should remember that the scholarship application can only be submitted once, so errors discovered after submission may not be correctable.

Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship Deadline

Applications are currently closed and are scheduled to reopen in October 2026.

Maastricht University states that information concerning participating programmes for the 2027–2028 academic year will be available from 1 October 2026 onwards.

Applicants interested in the 2027–2028 scholarship should therefore begin preparing their academic documents, CV, potential referee and other supporting information ahead of the reopening.

The previous published cycle required candidates to apply for a participating master’s programme by 8 December 2025, while the scholarship application deadline was 1 February 2026.

Those dates relate to the previous 2026–2027 cycle and should not automatically be treated as the final deadlines for 2027–2028.

Prospective applicants should check Maastricht University’s official scholarship announcement after applications reopen in October 2026 for the confirmed 2027–2028 deadlines.

Maastricht University Scholarship Selection Process

The published selection procedure provides useful insight into how Maastricht University evaluates scholarship candidates.

Although dates may change for future application cycles, the process demonstrates that scholarship selection involves several stages.

Stage 1: Application Completeness Check

The Maastricht University International Services Desk first checks scholarship applications to determine whether they are complete.

This reinforces the importance of submitting every required document correctly.

Stage 2: Applications Are Sent to Faculties

Complete applications are forwarded to the relevant Maastricht University faculties.

Stage 3: Faculty Ranking

Each faculty evaluates candidates and selects and ranks its strongest scholarship applicants.

Under the published process, each faculty selected and ranked its top five scholarship applicants before sending them to the International Services Desk for a final check.

Stage 4: Final Checks and Interview Invitations

Following the faculty selections, the UM International Services Desk performs the relevant final checks.

Selected candidates are then invited to participate in an online interview.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to discuss their academic background, motivation, ambitions and suitability for the scholarship if shortlisted.

Stage 5: Final Application Status

Following interviews, candidates are informed about the status of their scholarship applications.

Possible outcomes include:

  • Selected
  • Waitlisted
  • Rejected

Waitlisted candidates may subsequently have their status changed to either selected or rejected.

Successful scholarship recipients receive additional information concerning the award, their arrival in Maastricht and the mandatory Pre-Academic Training programme.

Stage 6: Accepting the Scholarship

Successful candidates must formally accept the scholarship.

This requires signing and returning the scholarship award letter to the Maastricht University International Services Desk.

Candidates should carefully read all scholarship conditions before accepting the award, particularly requirements concerning accommodation, participation in training and ambassador responsibilities.

Mandatory Pre-Academic Training

The Maastricht University Pre-Academic Training programme forms a mandatory component of the NL-High Potential Scholarship.

For the published 2026–2027 cycle, this consisted of a two-week mandatory programme beginning in the first week of August 2026.

Candidates applying for 2027–2028 should check the updated dates once the next scholarship cycle is officially published.

How Competitive Is the Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship?

The scholarship is exceptionally competitive.

Maastricht University states that only approximately 2% of applicants are awarded the scholarship.

This means meeting the minimum eligibility criteria should not be confused with being guaranteed an award.

Strong candidates should aim to present an application that demonstrates:

  • Excellent academic achievement
  • Clear motivation for their chosen master’s programme
  • Strong reasons for pursuing study at Maastricht University
  • Evidence of personal and professional potential
  • A compelling case for scholarship support
  • High-quality recommendations
  • Careful attention to application instructions
  • A complete and professionally presented application package

Candidates should also make sure that the information provided throughout their application is consistent.

Why International Students Should Consider This Scholarship

The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship stands out because of the breadth of financial assistance provided.

Instead of offering only a partial tuition discount, the scholarship addresses several major expenses associated with international postgraduate study.

Successful candidates can receive support covering tuition fees, living expenses, insurance, visa costs, required training and specified programme expenses.

For talented students who might otherwise find studying in the Netherlands financially difficult, this level of funding can make postgraduate education substantially more accessible.

The opportunity also provides scholarship recipients with the experience of studying in an international university environment while participating in ambassador and academic-development activities.

Important Points Applicants Should Remember

Before preparing an application, prospective candidates should remember:

  • Only participating Maastricht University master’s programmes qualify.
  • Applicants need to apply for their master’s programme before completing the scholarship application.
  • A Maastricht University student number is required for the scholarship application.
  • Academic excellence is essential.
  • The published benchmark is a GPA equivalent to at least 7.5/10.
  • Supporting documentation explaining the applicant’s grading system is required.
  • The scholarship is extremely competitive.
  • Only around 2% of applicants are awarded funding.
  • The allocated scholarship accommodation is mandatory.
  • Airfare is not included.
  • Scholarship recipients have ambassador responsibilities.
  • Applicants must carefully prepare all documents before submission.
  • Applications are currently closed and are expected to reopen in October 2026.
  • Candidates interested in 2027–2028 should verify all updated requirements, amounts and deadlines once Maastricht University publishes the new application cycle.

FIND OUT MORE AND APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship 2027–2028 represents an outstanding funding opportunity for academically excellent international students who want to pursue a master’s degree in the Netherlands.

With extensive support covering tuition fees, living expenses, insurance, visa application costs and other specified academic expenses, the programme removes many of the major financial obstacles associated with studying abroad.

However, applicants should not underestimate the competition. Maastricht University indicates that only around 2% of applicants ultimately receive the scholarship, meaning candidates need more than basic eligibility to succeed. Academic excellence, a compelling motivation, strong supporting documents, a credible reference and strict compliance with application instructions can all play an important role in the selection process.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing early. Applications are currently closed and are scheduled to reopen in October 2026, while information on participating programmes for the 2027–2028 academic year is expected to be available from 1 October 2026 onwards.

Because scholarship amounts, programme eligibility, age cut-offs, document dates and application deadlines can change between academic years, candidates should verify the official Maastricht University 2027–2028 scholarship information when the new cycle opens before submitting an application.

item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming how people work, communicate, access services, make decisions, conduct businesses, manage resources, and interact with institutions. Yet as AI systems become increasingly influential, questions about responsibility, human dignity, cultural identity, trust, safety, and governance have become equally important.

A new international initiative, Anima Mundi: The Soul of the World Meets the Machine, is inviting start-ups, industries, researchers, designers, engineers, founders, young people, and communities from around the world to explore how cultural traditions, mythologies, cosmologies, and lived experiences can contribute to the governance of artificial intelligence.

The initiative calls on participants to bring the wisdom embedded in their own cultures into contemporary conversations about AI. Through digital art and written descriptions, participants are encouraged to connect cultural stories and traditions with real decisions being made by AI companies and private-sector teams today.

The initiative is presented by the AI Hub for Sustainable Development, a G7-endorsed, MIMIT-UNDP co-led initiative focused on accelerating sustainable AI-driven growth in Africa in alignment with the Italy-Africa Mattei Plan.

What Is the Anima Mundi AI Call About?

The central idea behind the initiative is that responsible AI should not be shaped exclusively by engineers, companies, governments, or technical specialists.

Instead, the organisers argue that communities possess forms of cultural, moral, philosophical, spiritual, social, and historical knowledge that can contribute to how societies think about the power and responsibilities associated with AI.

The call therefore asks participants to explore the relationship between culture and artificial intelligence.

It specifically encourages submissions that bring forward:

  • Mythologies
  • Cosmologies
  • Living cultural traditions
  • Stories about power and responsibility
  • Experiences of dignity and domination
  • Traditions concerning care and reciprocity
  • Community experiences with technology
  • Cultural perspectives on responsible decision-making
  • Experiences of how AI affects people and communities

The objective is not to identify one universal cultural answer to AI governance. Instead, the initiative seeks to create a broader international dialogue in which different communities can contribute their own perspectives on how AI should interact with human societies.

Why Is Cultural Wisdom Being Connected to AI?

The initiative is based on the idea that technological systems do not operate independently of society.

AI systems can influence decisions concerning areas such as:

  • Healthcare
  • Agriculture
  • Education
  • Financial services
  • Employment
  • Language and communication
  • Data infrastructure
  • Public services
  • Digital platforms
  • Credit decisions
  • Information access

For example, an algorithm may evaluate a person’s eligibility for a loan, influence the information presented to a child, provide advice to a farmer, translate a local language, or affect decisions made in a workplace.

These applications involve more than technical performance. They can also raise questions about fairness, accountability, dignity, participation, community interests, and who has the authority to make consequential decisions.

The Anima Mundi initiative therefore asks participants to consider what cultural traditions can teach contemporary AI developers about these questions.

As the organisers explain, people who have experienced AI directly already possess important knowledge about its governance. Someone whose loan was assessed by an algorithm, whose agricultural decisions were influenced by an AI system, whose language was translated through technology, or whose work was affected by an automated decision may have valuable insight into how AI should be governed.

The Meaning of “Anima Mundi”

The phrase Anima Mundi is Latin for “the soul of the world.”

The initiative uses the concept to express an understanding of the world as a living and interconnected whole rather than simply as collections of isolated objects or resources.

According to the initiative, this idea recognises that cultures carry different forms of knowledge and meaning through:

  • Stories
  • Ancestral traditions
  • Rivers and natural environments
  • Tools
  • Dance
  • Music
  • Speech
  • Art
  • Community practices

The concept is therefore used as a framework for bringing cultural knowledge into conversations about technology and AI governance.

Connection to the Vatican’s Anima Mundi Collection

The initiative also connects the contemporary AI project to the history of the Vatican’s Anima Mundi collection.

The source explains that a Universal Exposition held in 1925 resulted in approximately one hundred thousand works being brought to Rome from different parts of the world. A permanent ethnological collection subsequently developed from this material.

In 2019, the Vatican reopened the collection under the name Anima Mundi, presenting it as a living space intended to reconnect with the communities from which the cultural works originated.

The initiative draws on this historical idea of cultural reconnection to argue that traditions should not be treated as static or dead artefacts. Instead, they can remain relevant sources of knowledge for contemporary challenges, including AI governance.

Inspired by “Magnifica Humanitas”

The initiative states that it was inspired by Pope Leo XIV’s Magnifica Humanitas and presents two biblical images as a framework for thinking about technology and society.

The Tower of Babel

The first image is the Tower of Babel, which the initiative associates with technology built around:

  • Pride
  • Efficiency
  • Erasure of difference
  • Loss of common language
  • Dispersion and confusion

Within the initiative’s framing, Babel represents a technological approach that fails to sufficiently account for human diversity.

The Rebuilding of Jerusalem

The second image is the rebuilding of Jerusalem under Nehemiah.

This story is presented as an alternative model based on:

  • Shared reconstruction
  • Community participation
  • Collective responsibility
  • Recognition of different contributions
  • Inclusion
  • A commitment that no one is left behind

The initiative uses this contrast to highlight the possibility of treating cultural diversity as a resource for building better approaches to AI governance.

Who Is Being Invited to Participate?

The invitation is deliberately broad.

The initiative initially identifies AI start-ups and industries working in communities as important participants. However, the wider call welcomes submissions from people and organisations around the world.

The organisers specifically invite:

  • Young people
  • Engineers

What Kind of Submission Is Required?

The submission has two principal components:

1. A Digital Artwork

Participants must submit an artwork created in a digital visual medium.

The artwork is not simply intended to illustrate a cultural story independently. The initiative specifically asks for work that has been created in interaction with the machine, with technology functioning as a partner in the creative process.

The technology should therefore contribute to bringing the cultural lesson or insight into contemporary form.

2. A Written Description of Up to 500 Words

Each submission must also include a written description of up to 500 words.

The description can be written in any language of the participant’s choice.

The written submission should identify:

  • The myth, tradition, or cultural frame being used
  • The AI decision or situation being examined
  • Why the myth and AI situation have been paired
  • The difficult or consequential choice involved in the real-world situation

The written description is particularly important because it provides the governance context behind the artistic work.

The AI Decision Must Be Based on a Real-World Situation

One of the most important requirements is that the submission cannot simply describe a hypothetical AI scenario.

Each submission must connect its cultural or mythological frame to a real, named instance involving AI and the private sector.

The initiative identifies six concrete AI moments concerning trust and safety and requires participants to anchor their submissions to an actual situation.

The selected situation must involve:

  • A real start-up or private-sector team
  • An actual community
  • An AI-related decision or interaction
  • A real relationship between the technology provider and the community

The submission should explain what happened and how the relevant decision was made.

What Should the Written Explanation Cover?

The organisers provide a detailed framework for the written description.

Participants are expected to discuss the governance dimension of the AI case alongside the cultural or mythological interpretation.

The write-up should address five major areas.

1. Design or Deployment Choices

Explain what decisions were made when the AI interaction was designed or deployed.

This could involve decisions about how a system interacts with users, what information it uses, what constraints are placed on it, or how a particular AI-enabled service is implemented.

2. Reasons Behind the Decisions

The participant should explain why the relevant decisions were made.

Possible factors identified by the initiative include:

  • Feedback from health workers
  • Internal safety practices
  • Regulation
  • Other forms of organisational or community input

3. People and Organisations Involved

The submission should identify the actors involved in the decision-making process.

These may include:

  • Community partners
  • Government ministries
  • Health ministries
  • Product teams
  • Industry partners
  • Other relevant stakeholders

4. Review and Oversight

The participant should explain how the decision was subsequently:

  • Reviewed
  • Overseen
  • Evaluated
  • Fed back into the AI system or development process

This helps demonstrate that AI governance is an ongoing process rather than a one-time technical decision.

5. Interpretation Through the Cultural Tradition

Finally, the participant should explain what the chosen myth, tradition, or cultural framework makes visible about the AI decision.

The submission should explore:

  • What the tradition helps people notice
  • What questions it raises
  • What assumptions it challenges
  • What lessons it carries forward
  • How it might contribute to thinking about responsible AI

The “Actors, Assets and Actions” Framework

For review purposes, the organisers state that submissions will be read through three questions.

Actors

Who was:

  • Involved?
  • Participating?
  • Responsible?
  • Accountable?

Assets

What exactly was being governed?

This could involve an AI system, data, an interaction, a service, a decision-making process, or another relevant technological asset.

Actions

What was:

  • Done?
  • Allowed?
  • Restricted?
  • Overridden?
  • Left undecided?

The framework also asks how local or cultural wisdom can provide guidance concerning these actions.

Why Communities Are Central to the Initiative

A major principle behind the call is that responsible AI cannot be developed solely through government regulation or private-sector decision-making.

The initiative recognises the important role of governments in building public trust in AI. However, it argues that governments cannot address every dimension of AI governance on their own.

Industry is also presented as an essential stakeholder because companies developing AI tools and solutions have direct knowledge of how these systems are being built, deployed, and experienced.

At the same time, the initiative argues that government and industry together cannot fully provide something that communities possess: long-established moral and cultural traditions concerning what power owes to the people affected by it.

This is why community knowledge and lived experience are placed at the centre of the call.

The Role of Mythology in AI Governance

The initiative’s use of mythology is not simply an artistic exercise.

Instead, mythology is presented as a way of asking questions about contemporary technological decisions.

Traditional stories can contain longstanding reflections on:

  • Power
  • Responsibility
  • Authority
  • Care
  • Reciprocity
  • Domination
  • Dignity
  • Community
  • Human relationships
  • The consequences of decisions

By bringing these stories into conversation with AI, participants can examine technological decisions from perspectives that may not emerge through technical analysis alone.

The purpose is therefore to create a dialogue between ancient or living cultural knowledge and contemporary technological systems.

What Happens to Submitted Works?

The initiative states that all works received will be preserved in a permanent, open online library.

The library is intended to function as a global commons containing traditions and testimonies relating to AI.

This means that the initiative is not simply seeking submissions for a temporary exhibition. The submitted works are intended to contribute to a longer-term collection of cultural perspectives on artificial intelligence.

Conclusion

The Anima Mundi: The Soul of the World Meets the Machine initiative creates an international platform for connecting cultural knowledge with contemporary debates about artificial intelligence. Rather than treating AI governance solely as a technical or regulatory challenge, the initiative invites participants to examine how mythology, cultural traditions, lived experience, community knowledge, and long-standing ideas about power and responsibility can inform decisions involving AI.

Participants are asked to go beyond abstract discussions by identifying a real-world AI decision involving a private-sector team and an actual community, and then interpreting that situation through a cultural or mythological lens. The resulting digital artwork and written explanation are intended to contribute to a permanent open online library documenting diverse perspectives on AI.

The call is open to participants worldwide, with particular invitations to the G7 and the 18 African partner countries of the Italy-Africa Mattei Plan. Young engineers, designers, researchers, founders, start-ups, industries, and people with direct experience of AI are specifically encouraged to participate.

For anyone interested in artificial intelligence, AI governance, digital transformation, cultural heritage, technology ethics, responsible innovation, community participation, African innovation, or the relationship between technology and society, the initiative offers a distinctive opportunity to place cultural knowledge directly into contemporary conversations about how AI should be developed and governed.
